mainTopic: Aggadic praise of מתן תורה: ישראל's bond with הקב"ה, the overwhelming power of each divine word at סיני, and משה's answer to the angels who objected to giving the Torah to humans.
overview: This amud is all אגדה, with no legal discussion. It opens with the end of רבא's answer to a heretic who mocked ישראל for saying נעשה ונשמע: wholehearted trust guides the upright. A chain of teachings follows. Keeping the מצוות deepens God's love. עולא compares the עגל to a bride betraying her husband under the חופה, while רב notes that the gentle wording of the פסוק shows הקב"ה still loves us. The גמרא then praises the words of מתן תורה. Each word split into seventy languages, Torah is like a ruler that can give life or death, and each word was crowned with two crowns. רבי יהושע בן לוי reads פסוקים in שיר השירים as Israel's loyalty through suffering and as forgiveness for the עגל. He also describes the overwhelming power of each word at סיני: it filled the world with fragrance, made the people's souls leave them, and drove them back twelve מיל. The amud ends with the story of משה going up to heaven, where the angels object to giving the Torah to humans. משה answers that its commandments only fit people, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's final answer to the heretic: integrity guides the wholehearted
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his reply to the צדוקי. People like us, who walk with wholeheartedness, are guided by our integrity. People who walk in deceit are destroyed by their crookedness.
steps.simpleTranslation: We, who walk with wholeheartedness, have this verse written about us: 'The integrity of the upright will guide them.' Those people who walk in deceit have this verse written about them: 'And the crookedness of the faithless will destroy them.'
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of רבא's answer to a heretic who called ישראל a 'hasty nation' for saying נעשה before נשמע. רבא closes the story by quoting a פסוק from משלי that contrasts the trusting with the deceitful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heretic thought it was foolish to accept the Torah before hearing its contents. רבא turns this around. Committing out of trust (תמימות) is not reckless, because that very integrity is what guides and protects a person. Only those who approach with trickery are harmed by it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's answer: accepting the Torah with נעשה ונשמע is not hasty. It is the wholehearted trust that guides and protects the upright.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-sentence. The word 'דסגינן' means 'we who walk' and is the end of רבא's reply ('אנן דסגינן...'), which began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: (We) who walk with wholeheartedness
it is written about us:
'The integrity of the upright will guide them,'
those people who walk in deceit,
it is written about them:
'And the crookedness of the faithless will destroy them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּסָגֵינַן בִּשְׁלִימוּתָא כְּתִיב בַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the story of רבא and the צדוקי that began on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Wholehearted trust in הקב"ה guides the upright, while deceit destroys the faithless.

steps.title: Accepting the Torah wins one eye; doing it wins both
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains a פסוק in שיר השירים. When ישראל first accepted the Torah, they won God's heart 'with one eye.' When they actually do the מצוות, it will be 'with both eyes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: What does the verse mean, 'You captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you captured my heart with one of your eyes'? At first, it was with one of your eyes. Once you actually perform the מצוות, it will be with both of your eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement praises ישראל's acceptance of the Torah. רבי יונתן reads 'one of your eyes' as only the first stage of God's love.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'one' tells us there is a fuller level still to come. Saying נעשה ונשמע earned partial love (one eye). Actually carrying out the מצוות completes it (both eyes). Commitment is precious, but action is the full expression.

keyTerms.meaning: When you will actually do (the מצוות)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
Rabbi Yonatan said:
What is (the meaning of) that which is written:
'You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride;
you have captured my heart with one of your eyes'?
At first (when you accepted the Torah), with one of your eyes;
when you actually perform (the מצוות), with both of your eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״לִבַּבְתִּנִי אֲחוֹתִי כַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of ישראל's acceptance of the Torah from רבא's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Accepting the Torah earned partial love. Fulfilling it earns complete love.

steps.title: עולא: the עגל was a bride betraying under her חופה
steps.stepSummary: עולא describes the חטא העגל, which happened right at מתן תורה, as a shameless bride who is unfaithful while still under her wedding canopy.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Shameless is the bride who is unfaithful while still under her wedding canopy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from praising ישראל to a sharp criticism. עולא compares the עגל, made just weeks after סיני, to betrayal during the wedding itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מתן תורה is pictured as the wedding between הקב"ה and ישראל. Sinning with the עגל so soon afterward is like a bride betraying her husband at the חופה, which makes the sin especially shocking.
steps.confusionAlert: עולא does not name the עגל explicitly, but that is what he means. The 'חופה' is מתן תורה.

phrases.english: Ulla said: Shameless is the bride
who is unfaithful within her wedding canopy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: עֲלוּבָה כַּלָּה מְזַנָּה בְּתוֹךְ חוּפָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'bride' imagery as step 2, but to criticize rather than praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חטא העגל was like betrayal during the wedding itself.

steps.title: The verse behind עולא's statement
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי provides a פסוק as the source for עולא's idea: 'While the king was still at his table, my spikenard gave off its fragrance.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, son of the daughter of שמואל, said: What verse hints at this? 'While the king was still at his table, my spikenard (gave off its fragrance)...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי asks which פסוק supports עולא's picture and answers with a verse from שיר השירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'While the king was still at his table' matches 'under the חופה', meaning while הקב"ה was still present at סיני. The spikenard 'giving off' its scent is read as its good fragrance leaving, which hints at the sin of the עגל.

keyTerms.meaning: At his table, at his feast

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of the daughter of Shmuel, said:
What verse (alludes to this)?
'While the king was still at his table, my spikenard, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a scriptural source for עולא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's claim that ישראל sinned with the עגל while still 'under the חופה'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים 1:12, 'עד שהמלך במסבו נרדי נתן ריחו'.

steps.title: רב: the gentle wording shows God still loves us
steps.stepSummary: רב notices that the פסוק says the fragrance was 'given' and not that it 'reeked'. This shows that even after the sin, הקב"ה still holds us dear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: And still, there is affection toward us, for it is written 'gave' (its fragrance), and it is not written 'reeked'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב softens the harsh picture by focusing on the exact wording of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said the spikenard 'stank', but it chose the gentle word 'נתן' instead. That delicate choice of words shows ongoing love: even when describing the עגל, the Torah speaks kindly of ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Gave off a foul odor, reeked

steps.whatToRemember: Even when the Torah speaks of the חטא העגל, it uses gentle language, which shows הקב"ה's love was never removed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: וַעֲדַיִין חַבִּיבוּתָא הִיא גַּבַּן,
phrases.english: Rav said: And still, affection is with us,
for it is written 'gave',
and it is not written 'reeked'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲדַיִין חַבִּיבוּתָא הִיא גַּבַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק from step 4 and draws a comforting message from its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The euphemism 'נתן' shows הקב"ה's continuing love for ישראל.

steps.title: Those who are insulted and stay silent shine like the sun
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא praises people who are insulted but do not insult back, who hear their shame and do not reply, who serve out of love and are happy even in suffering. They are like the sun rising in its strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Those who are insulted but do not insult, who hear their shame and do not respond, who act out of love and rejoice in suffering, about them the verse says: 'And those who love Him are like the sun going out in its might.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that praises humble, loving endurance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same word, 'עלובין', that עולא used, which links it to the previous discussion. Here it describes people who quietly accept humiliation and suffering out of love. Such people are compared to the powerful, shining sun.

keyTerms.meaning: Their shame, the insults against them

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the מידה of quietly bearing insult and accepting suffering with love.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Those who are insulted but do not insult,
who hear their shame and do not respond,
who act out of love and rejoice in suffering,
about them the verse says:
'And those who love Him are like the sun going out in its might.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֲלוּבִין וְאֵינָן עוֹלְבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected by the word 'עלובין' and by the theme of love that endures through hardship.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who suffer insult silently and serve with love are like the shining sun.

steps.title: Each word at Sinai split into seventy languages
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads a פסוק in תהילים to mean that every word הקב"ה spoke at סיני divided into seventy languages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What does the verse mean, 'The Lord gives the word; those who announce it are a great host'? Each and every word that came out of the mouth of the Almighty was divided into seventy languages.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens about the miracle of מתן תורה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A great host' of announcers is read as the many languages into which each divine word spread. The Torah was given in a way that was meant to reach all the nations of the world.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: What is (the meaning of) that which is written:
'The Lord gives the word;
those who proclaim the tidings are a great host'?
Each and every utterance
that came out of the mouth of the Almighty
was divided into seventy languages.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״ה׳ יִתֶּן אֹמֶר הַמְבַשְּׂרוֹת צָבָא רָב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the bond between God and ישראל to the nature of the revelation at סיני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every divine word at סיני split into seventy languages.

steps.title: Like a hammer shattering a rock into sparks
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches the same idea from ירמיהו. Just as a hammer striking rock sends out many sparks, each divine word split into seventy languages.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And like a hammer that shatters a rock.' Just as this hammer breaks into many sparks, so too each and every word that came out of the mouth of הקדוש ברוך הוא was divided into seventy languages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source that supports רבי יוחנן's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a parallel derivation from a different פסוק. A single blow from a hammer produces many sparks, and in the same way a single divine word produced many languages. The image strengthens רבי יוחנן's idea.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'And like a hammer that shatters a rock':

phrases.aramaic: מָה פַּטִּישׁ זֶה נֶחֱלָק לְכַמָּה נִיצוֹצוֹת —
phrases.english: just as this hammer breaks into several sparks,
so too each and every utterance
that came out of the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
was divided into seventy languages.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: ״וּכְפַטִּישׁ יְפֹצֵץ סָלַע״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel source for the same idea taught in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that each divine word split into seventy languages.

steps.title: Torah is like a ruler that can kill or give life
steps.stepSummary: רב חננאל בר פפא explains why the Torah's words are called 'נגידים' (royal/ruling things). Like a ruler, the Torah has power to bring death or life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חננאל בר פפא said: What does the verse mean, 'Listen, for I will speak royal things'? Why are words of Torah compared to a ruler? To teach you: just as this ruler has power to kill and to give life, so too words of Torah have power to kill and to give life.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement explains the word 'נגידים' in a פסוק from משלי as comparing Torah to a ruler.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruler holds power over life and death. The Torah is equally powerful: it can give life or bring death, depending on how a person relates to it. The next step explains how this works.

keyTerms.meaning: To kill and to give life

phrases.english: Rav Chananel bar Pappa said:
What is (the meaning of) that which is written: 'Listen, for I will speak royal things'?
Why are words of Torah compared to a ruler?
To tell you:

phrases.aramaic: מָה נָגִיד זֶה יֵשׁ בּוֹ לְהָמִית וּלְהַחֲיוֹת,
phrases.english: just as this ruler has (power) to kill and to give life,

phrases.aramaic: אַף דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה יֶשׁ בָּם לְהָמִית וּלְהַחֲיוֹת.
phrases.english: so too words of Torah have (power) to kill and to give life.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״שִׁמְעוּ כִּי נְגִידִים אֲדַבֵּר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues praising the power of דברי תורה with a new פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah, like a ruler, has power over life and death.

steps.title: רבא: Torah is a drug of life or of death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא's well-known saying fits this idea. For those who approach Torah 'with the right hand' it is a medicine of life, and for those who approach it 'with the left hand' it is a drug of death.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבא said: To those who go 'right-handed' with it, it is a drug of life. To those who go 'left-handed' with it, it is a drug of death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses 'היינו דאמר' to show that רבא's saying expresses the same idea as רב חננאל's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step explains how Torah can kill or give life. It depends on the learner's approach. Learning with full effort and pure intentions (the 'right hand') brings life. Learning carelessly or with bad motives (the 'left hand') brings harm.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what (so-and-so) said, the same idea

steps.whatToRemember: The same Torah can be life-giving or harmful. It depends on whether one learns it properly (לשמה, with full effort) or not.

phrases.english: This is what Rava said:
To those who go right-handed with it, (it is) a drug of life;
to those who go left-handed with it, (it is) a drug of death.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corroborates and explains step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רב חננאל's claim that Torah can kill or give life.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's saying about 'סמא דחיי' and 'סמא דמותא'.

steps.title: Another reading: two crowns for every divine word
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation of 'נגידים' (royal): to every word הקב"ה spoke at סיני, two crowns were tied.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Royal things' means that to each and every word that came out of the mouth of הקדוש ברוך הוא, two crowns are tied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different interpretation of the same word 'נגידים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'royal' refers to crowns rather than to power over life and death. Each divine word was crowned with two crowns, honoring the Torah's royal status, the way a king is honored with a crown.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'Royal things':
each and every utterance
that came out of the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
two crowns are tied to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״נְגִידִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative reading of 'נגידים' from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each divine word at סיני was crowned with two crowns.

steps.title: Even when God causes me bitterness, He stays close
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads 'צרור המור' as כנסת ישראל saying: even though my Beloved causes me pain and bitterness, He still rests close to my heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What does the verse mean, 'A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me; he shall lie between my breasts'? כנסת ישראל said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: רבונו של עולם, even though my Beloved causes me distress and bitterness, 'He lies between my breasts.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement reads a פסוק in שיר השירים as Israel's loyal love despite suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מור' (myrrh) sounds like 'מר', meaning bitter. The 'צרור' (bundle) sounds like 'מיצר', meaning causing distress. Even when הקב"ה brings hardship, ישראל keeps Him close to her heart, which echoes the ברייתא in step 6 about rejoicing in suffering.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is (the meaning of) that which is written:
'A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me;
he shall lie between my breasts'?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּיצֵר וּמֵימֵר לִי דּוֹדִי —
phrases.english: even though my Beloved causes me distress and bitterness,
'He lies between my breasts.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״צְרוֹר הַמּוֹר דּוֹדִי לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the theme of the loving bond between ישראל and הקב"ה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראל keeps הקב"ה close even when He brings suffering.

steps.title: The One who owns everything forgives the sin of the עגל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי continues with the next פסוק. 'אשכול הכופר... כרמי עין גדי' is read as: the One to whom everything belongs forgives me for the sin of the 'kid' (the עגל) that I gathered for myself.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A cluster of henna is my beloved to me, in the vineyards of עין גדי.' The One to whom everything belongs forgives me for the sin of the kid that I gathered for myself.
steps.whatsHappening: The same אמורא reads the next פסוק through wordplay as a message of forgiveness for the עגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is read by its sound. 'אשכול' becomes 'שהכל שלו' (everything is His). 'הכופר' becomes 'מכפר' (forgives). 'גדי' (kid) stands for the calf. 'כרמי' becomes 'שכרמתי' (that I gathered). The sin of the עגל, which עולא described so harshly, is forgiven.
steps.whatToRemember: The sequence closes the circle: עולא described the עגל as betrayal at the חופה, and רבי יהושע בן לוי shows that הקב"ה forgives it.

phrases.english: 'A cluster of henna is my beloved to me,
in the vineyards of Ein Gedi':
He to Whom everything belongs
forgives me for the sin of the kid
that I gathered for myself.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אֶשְׁכֹּל הַכֹּפֶר דּוֹדִי לִי בְּכַרְמֵי עֵין גֶּדִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading with the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב"ה, who owns everything, forgives ישראל for the עגל.

steps.title: How do we know 'כרמי' means gathering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the word 'כרמי' can mean 'gathering'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is it understood that this word 'כרמי' is a term for gathering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question one word in the previous interpretation. The next step will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally 'כרמי' means 'vineyards'. Step 13 read it as 'gathered', so the גמרא wants proof that the root can carry that meaning.

phrases.english: From where is it understood that this 'karmei'
is a term of gathering?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי ״כַּרְמֵי״ לִישָּׁנָא דְמִכְנַשׁ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the word-meaning used in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the root כרם can mean 'to gather'.

steps.title: Proof from the launderer's chair in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא brings a משנה that mentions a launderer's chair 'on which one gathers (כורמים) the garments', proving the root can mean gathering.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, son of רב נחמן, said: As we learned in a משנה: A launderer's chair on which one gathers the garments.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers the question by pointing to a משנה where the same root clearly means gathering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses 'כורמים' for piling up clothes on a launderer's chair. This shows that 'כרם' can mean gathering, which supports reading 'כרמי' as 'שכרמתי', the gathering of gold for the עגל.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Nachman, said:
As we learned (in a Mishnah):
A launderer's chair
on which one gathers the garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן, כְּדִתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה about a launderer's chair uses 'כורמים' to mean gathering garments, so 'כרמי' can mean gathering.

steps.title: Every divine word filled the world with fragrance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads 'לחייו כערוגת הבושם' as describing how each utterance at סיני filled the whole world with spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What does the פסוק 'His cheeks are like a bed of spices' mean? With each and every word that came out of the mouth of הקדוש ברוך הוא, the whole world was filled with sweet spices.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives another teaching from שיר השירים about מתן תורה. He says every word הקדוש ברוך הוא spoke filled the world with a beautiful smell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Cheeks' are read as the place speech comes from, which is God's mouth. So 'a bed of spices' becomes a description of what His words produced: fragrance filling the entire world. This sets up a question, because if the first word already filled the world, where was there room for more?

keyTerms.meaning: His cheeks (read as His mouth, the source of His speech)
an utterance or spoken word (here, the words at סיני)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said,
What is the meaning of what is written:
"His cheeks are like a bed of spices" —
each and every utterance
that came out of the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
the entire world was filled with spices.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of רבי יהושע בן לוי's readings of שיר השירים as describing מתן תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each divine utterance at סיני filled the whole world with fragrance.

steps.title: Where did the second word's fragrance go?
steps.stepSummary: If the first utterance already filled the world with spices, where was there room for the fragrance of the second utterance?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the world was already full from the first word, where did the second word's fragrance go?
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching raises a logical problem with its own picture. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the world is 'full', no space is left. So the question is how each later utterance could still fill the world with its own fragrance.

phrases.english: And since it was filled from the first utterance,
where did the second utterance go?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁמִּדִּיבּוּר רִאשׁוֹן נִתְמַלֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a logical difficulty inside the picture given in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How there was room for the fragrance of each later utterance once the world was already full.

steps.title: A wind cleared each fragrance away to make room
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא brought out a wind that carried away each fragrance in turn, learned from 'שושנים' read as 'ששונים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא brought a wind out of His storehouses, and it moved away each fragrance, one after another. As it says: 'His lips are lilies, dripping flowing myrrh.' Don't read it 'שושנים' (lilies); read it 'ששונים' (that repeat).
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question. A divine wind cleared out each fragrance so the next word could fill the world again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses two words in the פסוק. 'מור עובר' (flowing, passing myrrh) shows that the fragrance passed away. Reading 'שושנים' as 'ששונים' (repeating) shows that this happened again and again, once for each word.

keyTerms.meaning: don't read it as... (a reading for a דרשה, not a change to the text)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the פסוק is spelled wrong. It is a דרשה technique that reads extra meaning into the same letters.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹצִיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הָרוּחַ מֵאוֹצְרוֹתָיו
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, brought out the wind from His storehouses
and it would carry away each one, one after another,
as it is stated:
"His lips are lilies, dripping flowing myrrh."
(Do not read "shoshanim" [lilies], but rather "sheshonim" [that repeat].)

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹצִיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הָרוּחַ מֵאוֹצְרוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A divine wind cleared away each fragrance in turn, so every utterance could fill the world anew.

steps.title: With every divine word, ישראל's souls left them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that at each utterance the souls of ישראל left their bodies, based on 'נפשי יצאה בדברו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: With each and every word that came out of the mouth of הקדוש ברוך הוא, the souls of ישראל left them. As it says: 'My soul left when He spoke.'
steps.whatsHappening: Here is a new teaching from רבי יהושע בן לוי. Hearing God's voice directly was so overwhelming that the people's souls left their bodies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in שיר השירים, 'נפשי יצאה בדברו', is read literally. The soul departed as He spoke. This again sets up a question about the words that came afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: my soul left when He spoke

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל דִּיבּוּר וְדִיבּוּר שֶׁיָּצָא מִפִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: With each and every utterance that came out of the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
the souls of Israel left,
as it is stated: "My soul departed when He spoke."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל דִּיבּוּר וְדִיבּוּר שֶׁיָּצָא מִפִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching in the same series about the effect of each utterance at סיני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At each utterance at סיני, the souls of ישראל left their bodies.

steps.title: How could they hear the second word?
steps.stepSummary: If their souls left at the first utterance, how did they receive the second one?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since their souls already left at the first word, how did they receive the second word?
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching asks an obvious problem with its own claim. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the people were lifeless after the first utterance, they could not have heard and accepted the next ones. Something must have restored them.

phrases.english: And since their souls left from the first utterance,
how did they receive the second utterance? —

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁמִּדִּיבּוּר רִאשׁוֹן יָצְתָה נִשְׁמָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a logical difficulty inside the claim of step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How ישראל could hear the later utterances after their souls had left.

steps.title: God revived them with the dew of תחיית המתים
steps.stepSummary: God brought down the dew that will revive the dead in the future and brought them back to life, based on 'גשם נדבות תניף אלהים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought down the dew that will one day bring the dead back to life, and He revived them. As it says: 'You, God, poured down a generous rain; when Your inheritance was weary, You strengthened it.'
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question. God revived the people with the special dew of תחיית המתים so they could hear the next word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'generous rain' in תהלים is taken as the reviving dew. 'Your inheritance' means ישראל. 'Weary' means they had collapsed, and 'You strengthened it' means God restored them to life.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹרִיד טַל שֶׁעָתִיד לְהַחֲיוֹת בּוֹ מֵתִים
phrases.english: He brought down the dew with which He will in the future revive the dead
and He revived them,
as it is stated: "You, God, poured down a generous rain;
Your inheritance, when it was weary, You sustained it."

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹרִיד טַל שֶׁעָתִיד לְהַחֲיוֹת בּוֹ מֵתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God revived them with the dew of תחיית המתים after each utterance.

steps.title: ישראל retreated twelve מיל, and angels walked them back
steps.stepSummary: At each utterance ישראל recoiled twelve מיל, and the מלאכי השרת helped them walk back, reading 'ידודון' as 'ידדון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: With each and every word that came out of the mouth of הקדוש ברוך הוא, ישראל moved back twelve מיל, and the ministering angels helped them walk back. As it says: 'The angels of hosts ידודון ידודון.' Don't read it 'ידודון' (they flee); read it 'ידדון' (they help walk).
steps.whatsHappening: This is another teaching in the series. Out of awe, the people pulled back a great distance at every word, and angels guided them back to the mountain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק says the angels 'flee'. The אל תקרי reading turns it into 'they lead along', like helping someone take steps. The people pulled back on their own out of fear, and the angels' job was to walk them back to the mountain.

keyTerms.meaning: a unit of distance, about a kilometer
helping someone walk step by step

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל דִּיבּוּר וְדִיבּוּר שֶׁיָּצָא מִפִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: With each and every utterance that came out of the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: חָזְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲחוֹרֵיהֶן שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִיל
phrases.english: Israel retreated backward twelve mil
and the ministering angels would walk them back,
as it is stated: "The angels of hosts flee, they flee" —
do not read "yidodun" [they flee], but rather "yedadun" [they lead them along].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל דִּיבּוּר וְדִיבּוּר שֶׁיָּצָא מִפִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָזְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third teaching about the overwhelming effect of each utterance at סיני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At each utterance ישראל recoiled twelve מיל, and angels led them back.

steps.title: The angels ask why a human is in heaven
steps.stepSummary: When משה went up, the angels asked what a person born of a woman was doing among them. הקדוש ברוך הוא answered that he came to receive the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: When משה went up to heaven, the ministering angels said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: 'Master of the world, what is a human born from a woman doing among us?' He told them: 'He came to receive the תורה.'
steps.whatsHappening: A famous story begins. The angels are surprised to see a human in heaven, and God explains that משה came to receive the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'born of a woman' stresses that משה is physical and mortal, unlike the angels. God's answer that he came for the תורה sets up the angels' real objection in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: one born of a woman, a human being

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
When Moses ascended on High,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: the ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, מַה לִּילוּד אִשָּׁה בֵּינֵינוּ?
phrases.english: Master of the Universe, what is one born of a woman doing among us?
He said to them: He came to receive the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁעָלָה מֹשֶׁה לַמָּרוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story by רבי יהושע בן לוי about משה receiving the תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angels questioned משה's presence in heaven, and God said he came to receive the תורה.

steps.title: The angels object to giving the תורה to humans
steps.stepSummary: The angels argue that the hidden treasure, stored for 974 generations before creation, should not go to flesh and blood, and that it belongs in heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said before Him: 'A hidden treasure that You stored away for 974 generations before the world was created, You want to give it to flesh and blood? "What is man that You remember him, and the son of man that You pay attention to him?" "ה׳ our Lord, how mighty is Your name in all the earth, place Your glory upon the heavens!"'
steps.whatsHappening: The angels challenge God's decision. They argue that the precious, ancient תורה is too lofty for mortals and should stay in heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack has two parts. First, the תורה's great value and age make mortals unworthy of it. Second, they quote תהלים ח: man is insignificant, and God's 'glory', meaning the תורה, belongs 'on the heavens', with the angels.
steps.confusionAlert: The number 974 comes from 'a thousand generations' (תהלים קה:ח). The תורה was given in the 26th generation from אדם, so the other 974 generations are counted as coming before creation.

phrases.english: They said before Him: A hidden treasure

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁגְּנוּזָה לָךְ תְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת וְשִׁבְעִים וְאַרְבָּעָה דּוֹרוֹת
phrases.english: that was stored away by You for nine hundred and seventy-four generations
before the world was created,
You seek to give it to flesh and blood?
"What is man that You are mindful of him,
and the son of man that You think of him?"

phrases.aramaic: ״ה׳ אֲדֹנֵינוּ מָה אַדִּיר שִׁמְךָ בְּכׇל הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: "Lord our Master, how glorious is Your name in all the earth,
place Your majesty upon the heavens!"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לְפָנָיו: חֶמְדָּה גְּנוּזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The angels respond to God's answer by objecting to it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to give the תורה to משה and humanity.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something so precious and ancient belongs in heaven, not with insignificant mortals.

steps.title: God tells משה to answer, holding the Throne for protection
steps.stepSummary: God asks משה to answer the angels. משה fears being burned, so God tells him to grasp the Throne of Glory, supported by a פסוק in איוב and רבי נחום's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה: 'Give them an answer.' משה said: 'Master of the world, I'm afraid they will burn me with the breath of their mouths.' He said: 'Hold on to My Throne of Glory and answer them.' As it says: 'He holds the face of the Throne, He spreads His cloud over him.' And רבי נחום said: this teaches that שדי spread some of the glow of His שכינה and His cloud over him.
steps.whatsHappening: Before משה answers, the scene is set. God gives משה protection so he can safely respond to the angels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'פרשז' is read as a combination of 'פירש שדי זיו', meaning 'שדי spread radiance'. So the פסוק describes God covering משה with His glory and cloud. This step prepares for משה's actual answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a rare word, read as 'פירש שדי זיו' (שדי spread radiance)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses:
Give them an answer.
He said before Him: Master of the Universe,

phrases.aramaic: מִתְיָירֵא אֲנִי שֶׁמָּא יִשְׂרְפוּנִי בַּהֶבֶל שֶׁבְּפִיהֶם.
phrases.english: I am afraid that they may burn me with the breath of their mouths.
He said to him: Grasp My Throne of Glory
and give them an answer.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מְאַחֵז פְּנֵי כִּסֵּא פַּרְשֵׁז עָלָיו עֲנָנוֹ״,
phrases.english: As it is stated: "He causes him to grasp the face of the throne, and spreads His cloud over him,"
and Rabbi Nachum said:

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁפֵּירַשׂ שַׁדַּי מִזִּיו שְׁכִינָתוֹ וַעֲנָנוֹ עָלָיו.
phrases.english: This teaches that the Almighty spread of the radiance of His Presence and His cloud over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה: הַחְזֵיר לָהֶן תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: God turns the angels' objection over to משה to answer, and provides him protection.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה answered the angels while grasping the Throne, protected by the radiance of the שכינה.

steps.title: משה's first answer: you were never slaves in מצרים
steps.stepSummary: משה points out that the first דיבור speaks of leaving מצרים, which never applied to angels, so the תורה is not for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה said: 'Master of the world, the תורה You are giving me, what is written in it?' 'I am ה׳ your God who took you out of the land of מצרים.' He said to the angels: 'Did you go down to מצרים? Were you slaves to פרעה? Why should the תורה be yours?'
steps.whatsHappening: משה begins answering the angels' objection. He shows that the very first commandment is addressed to people who lived through slavery, not to angels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה flips the angels' argument. They said the תורה is too lofty for humans. משה shows that its content is built for human experience, so it does not fit angels at all.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe,

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹרָה שֶׁאַתָּה נוֹתֵן לִי מָה כְּתִיב בָּהּ?
phrases.english: the Torah that You are giving me, what is written in it?
"I am the Lord your God
who brought you out of the land of Egypt."
He said to them: Did you go down to Egypt?
Were you enslaved to Pharaoh?
Why should the Torah be yours!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, תּוֹרָה שֶׁאַתָּה נוֹתֵן לִי מָה כְּתִיב בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: משה, now protected, begins answering the angels' objection from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the תורה's content applies only to humans.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The angels thought the תורה is too lofty for mortals and belongs in heaven.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה addresses human history, such as slavery in מצרים, so it was never meant for angels.

steps.title: משה's second answer: you don't live among idol worshippers
steps.stepSummary: משה cites 'לא יהיה לך אלהים אחרים' and begins arguing that angels don't live among nations that worship idols. This passage cuts off mid-sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: Again: 'What is written in it?' 'You shall not have other gods.' 'Do you live among the nations, who worship...'
steps.whatsHappening: משה continues with a second commandment to show that it, too, only makes sense for humans. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ban on idol worship only matters for someone exposed to idol worshippers. Angels live in heaven, not among the nations, so this מצוה does not apply to them.

phrases.english: Again: What is written in it?
"You shall have no other gods."
Do you dwell among the nations, who worship
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב: מָה כְּתִיב בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues משה's answer with a second commandment.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second example showing that the תורה's commandments are for humans.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban on idolatry only applies to those living among idol worshippers, which is humans, not angels.
